title: Why Postal Employees Go Postal
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the "going postal" phrase and the phenomenon of U.S. Postal Service workers committing workplace shootings, mainly in the 1980s and 1990s. They recount the 1986 Edmond, Oklahoma post office shooting by Patrick Henry Sherrill, other incidents including Thomas McIlvaine's Michigan shooting, the 1993 cases, and Jennifer San Marcos's 2006 Goleta, California rampage. They cover the 1993 newspaper citation and Seinfeld and Simpsons references, the Califano Commission report that called "going postal" a myth, critics like Stephen Misasko who said it was real, and the postal culture, grievance backlog, and neoliberal changes after the 1971 Postal Reorganization Act. The episode closes with listener mail about safe cracking, including the Little Joker and Max Shinburn.

segments.title: Opening banter and going postal band names
segments.summary: Hosts chat about the length of the year, smoking at school and on planes, and find bands and businesses named Going Postal, noting the phrase's origin in workplace shootings.

segments.title: Patrick Henry Sherrill and the 1986 Edmond post office shooting
segments.summary: Patrick Henry Sherrill, a Edmond, Oklahoma postal carrier facing firing for poor performance, shot his postmaster and then killed fifteen people including himself in about fifteen minutes. Hosts note it was among the first workplace mass shootings to draw national attention.

segments.title: Early postal shootings and the rise of the phrase
segments.summary: Earlier postal shootings targeted supervisors and co-workers, and from 1986 to 1999 fifteen incidents killed thirty-four people. The phrase appeared in print in 1993 in a St. Petersburg Times article about a USPS workplace violence symposium.

segments.title: Seinfeld and Simpsons references
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the Seinfeld episode featuring Newman's postal worker rant and a Simpsons dream sequence with a mail carrier shooting back, showing how the idea had entered pop culture.

segments.title: Thomas McIlvaine and other cases
segments.summary: Thomas McIlvaine, a former Marine discharged dishonorably, shot up a Michigan post office in 1993, killing four and then himself. Coworkers described a toxic environment. Also covered: Larry Jason's 1993 shooting over a promotion and Mark Hilburn's stalking-related killings, and Jennifer San Marcos's 2006 Goleta, California rampage.

segments.title: Break and notary tangent
segments.summary: Hosts take a break and joke about Chuck becoming a notary, a minivan wrap, and Jerry's daughter speaking Spanish.

segments.title: Califano Commission and the myth claim
segments.summary: The USPS paid about four million dollars for a commission chaired by Joseph Califano Jr., which concluded going postal was a myth and that postal work was safe compared with taxi driving or convenience store work. Critics said the statistics were misleading.

segments.title: Stephen Misasko, postal culture, and neoliberalism
segments.summary: Stephen Misasko, a USPS workplace improvement analyst, argued worker-on-worker homicides were disproportionately postal. Surveys showed low morale, paramilitary management, grievance backlogs, and the 1971 Postal Reorganization Act's profit mandate was linked to neoliberal changes.

segments.title: Listener mail: safe cracking
segments.summary: A listener, co-host of The Heist podcast, corrects and adds details on safe cracking, including Mr X's torch cut, the Little Joker tool, and Max Shinburne's sabotage of Lily Safes.
